models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Benign night at Portorosa, light SSE for the 22 nm run to Lipari - leave 06:00 and expect to motor.
briefing.synopsis: No active pressure feature in the payload for the islands: the models show a slack, light-wind regime across the whole archipelago, 2-5 kt almost everywhere. ECMWF IFS (02 Oct 18Z), ECMWF AIFS (03 Oct 00Z) and ICON-2i (03 Oct 00Z) agree on a diurnal rotation rather than a gradient wind - SSE overnight and early morning, swinging through N/NE by midday and easing to 2-4 kt by evening. Seas are flat, 0.1 ft total wave and 0.1 ft swell at every island through 5 Oct in the consensus hourly data. The only meaningful change in the forecast period is later in the week, with W 10-14 kt and 2.2-2.6 ft on 9 Oct for the run home.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: Tonight is Portorosa Marina - enclosed, all-round shelter, and the only option listed. Consensus for the berth is 4.3 kt SE gusting 8.6 kt with 0.1 ft swell; the Portorosa hourly series shows 3.7 kt ENE gusting 11.7 at 18:00 easing to 3.6 kt SSE gusting 9.1 by midnight (ECMWF IFS 02 Oct 18Z / AIFS and ICON-2i 03 Oct 00Z consensus). Nothing in the payload would give the fleet a reason to move.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: Portorosa shows 4.6 kt from 178° (SSE) gusting 10.3 kt at 06:00, waves 0.1 ft. The computed window table makes 06:00 the recommended departure for Portorosa → Lipari, with 06:00 and 08:00 both at roughly 4-5 kt SSE, 0.1 ft, TWA 176-178 - a dead run in very light air, so plan on motor-sailing for most of the 22 nm. Windows stay open all day (all five rated go), but after 10:00 the breeze goes ENE then N at 2-4 kt with TWA 28, i.e. straight on the nose, so the early start is the better one. Gusts of 11-13 kt appear against 3-5 kt means; these are interval-maximum values from a single model in light air, reported but not flagged.

passage_notes.note: Depart 06:00: 4.6 kt SSE gusting 10.9, 0.1 ft, run. By midday the wind is N at 3-4 kt, TWA 28 - motoring. Verdict go on every window.
NW 4-5 kt all day, gusts under 11 kt, waves 0.1-0.2 ft, beam to close reach. Benign; departure time is a matter of preference.

NW 5-6.4 kt, gusts to 13.6 kt midday, waves building only to 0.5 ft by the 14:00 window. Berth at Marina del Gabbiano is rated workable, not sheltered - open from every direction and no anchoring - so it depends on it staying calm.

passage_notes.leg: Stromboli → Panarea, optional return (06 Oct, 11 nm)
passage_notes.note: 2-4 kt, gusts under 8 kt, 0.5-0.7 ft. Motoring passage. Panarea berths all rated sheltered at 6.2 kt S.
S-to-E 7-8 kt, gusts to 11.5, 1.0 ft - the best sailing of the week so far, close reach early turning broad reach to a run by afternoon.
SSW 5-6 kt in the morning falling to 2-3 kt after midday, 0.7-0.9 ft. Rinella is the recommended berth over Santa Marina, where 9 kt SSW blows straight in.
The windiest leg: W 10-14.4 kt gusting 19-23.7 kt, 2.2-2.6 ft, broad reach. Rated go throughout, but it is five days out and worth re-reading nearer the time.

cautions: Salina → Portorosa on 9 Oct shows gusts to 23.7 kt in the 08:00 window against a 13.6 kt mean, with 2.4 ft sea - the only leg in the payload with real breeze in it.
Marina del Gabbiano at Stromboli is open through 360° and marked no-anchoring; shelter there rests entirely on conditions staying as light as forecast.

In winds this light, direction is the unreliable part: the stability record shows mean direction shifts of 17-26 degrees at 0-48 h lead even where wind speed shifts average only 0.5 kt. Plan the sail plan loosely.
Verdicts in this payload are conservative threshold calculations, not decisions - the skipper's call stands.
briefing.confidence_note: IFS, AIFS and ICON-2i agree closely on a light-wind, flat-sea pattern for the next 48 h, and the stability record shows mean wind shifts of only 0.5 kt at 0-24 h lead; confidence drops for the 9 Oct leg at 72-120 h, where shifts average 0.9 kt and up to 3.9 kt with 61 degrees of direction scatter.

verification.measures: forecast stability, not verified accuracy - the reference is the newest model run for the same hour, not an observation
